In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
equivalent electric circuit modelling is a suitable approach to build battery models.
the equivalent electric circuit modelling is still the most popular and effective way to predict battery behaviour, and it will continue to be used for a long period of time.
there is no perfect modelling method, and the choice of a specific modelling method depends on the specific application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the modelling methods can be divided into three categories: equivalent circuit models, physical models, and artificial intelligence models.

a good battery model should have the following properties: a) the model should be able to predict the battery behaviour under various working conditions, b) the model should have a small number of parameters and be easy to implement, c) the model should not require much information from the battery, and d) the model should provide a physical interpretation of the battery behaviour.

the battery model can be built based on the electrochemical and electrical characteristics of the battery and the model parameters can be identified by the experimental data or by the electrochemical models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no one-size-fits-all battery model.
the equivalent electric circuit model is a simple and effective tool for predicting battery performance, and the model accuracy is strongly dependent on how well the model parameters are identified.

the equivalent electric circuit model should be carefully selected according to different battery operating conditions, and the model parameters should be identified with proper identification methods.
